## FA3 paged (PagedKVNonTMA, page_size=1) bf16 hd128 causal forward — SASS mainloop analysis

**Target binary:** `/home/yak/miniconda3/envs/dev/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/vllm_flash_attn/_vllm_fa3_C.abi3.so` (fat binary, 192 embedded `sm_90a` cubins).

### Kernel identification
Of 1166 `cutlass::device_kernel<flash::FlashAttnFwdSm90<…>>` symbols, the bf16/hd128/causal/paged one is (demangled, mainloop flags in order = `Is_causal, Is_local, Has_softcap, Varlen, PagedKVNonTMA, AppendKV, HasQv, MmaPV_is_RS, IntraWGOverlap, PackGQA, Split, V_colmajor`):

```
CollectiveMainloopFwdSm90<2, tuple<C<1>,C<1>,C<1>>, tuple<C<128>,C<128>,C<128>>, 128,
  bfloat16_t, float, Sm90,
  true, false, false, true, true, false, false, true, true, true, false, false,   // causal=1, PagedKVNonTMA=1
  bfloat16_t, 1>                                                                    // ElementSAux=bf16, kBlockH
```
i.e. `Stages=2`, `ClusterShape=1×1×1`, `TileShape=(kBlockM=128, kBlockN=128, kHeadDim=128)`. Four binary variants exist differing only in the trailing `kBlockH` GQA-pack factor (1/4/8/16) — identical KV-loop SASS. I dumped the `kBlockH=1` symbol via `cuobjdump -sass -fun <mangled>` (11,008 SASS instructions).

### Overall structure — warp-specialized producer/consumer with 3 consumer loops + 1 producer loop
The kernel branches on warpgroup role. Backward-branch loop bodies (loop latch → header):

| Loop | Span | HGMMA | EX2 | FSEL / ISETP.GT | LDGSTS | Role |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | `0x6980–0xb8a0` | 16 | 66 | 132 / 128 | 0 | consumer, causal-masked diagonal block |
| **B** | `0xb8d0–0xd6c0` | **16** | **66** | **0 / 0** | 0 | **consumer, unmasked interior block = STEADY STATE** |
| C | `0xdf0–0x10500` | 16 | 66 | 132 / 133 (+8 STSM) | 0 | consumer, peeled first/boundary block |
| D | `0x11310–0x14ef0` | 0 | 0 | – | 80 | **producer, cp.async KV loads** |

All 48 static HGMMA are `HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16` (m64 n128 k16, FP32 accum, BF16 in). Producer loads are 100% in loop D — **cp.async is NOT interleaved with HGMMA; it runs in a physically separate producer warpgroup** and hands off through mbarriers.

### Steady-state consumer iteration (loop B, 479 instrs) — per-iteration MIX

| Category | Count | Detail |
|---|---|---|
| **HGMMA** | **16** | 8× QK^T (`R24, gdesc[…], RZ/R24` — both operands smem) + 8× P·V (`R88, R152..R180, gdesc[…].tnspB, R88` — P from **registers** since MmaPV_is_RS=1, V read `.tnspB`). Each side = 8 k16 steps to cover the 128 contraction. |
| **MUFU.EX2** | **66** | ≈64 (one per S element/thread; the 64×128 tile → 64 elems/thread) + 2 running-max corrections. Base-2 exp with log2(e) folded into the QK scale. |
| **F2FP.BF16.F32.PACK_AB** | 32 | pack S→P (bf16) into registers for the *next* iteration's PV (IntraWGOverlap). |
| FP32 ALU | 266 | FMNMX.FTZ ×68 (row-max), FADD.FTZ ×64 (row-sum), FMUL.FTZ ×68 + FFMA.FTZ ×66 (scale/rescale). |
| **SHFL** | 4 | `SHFL.BFLY` — cross-thread max/sum reduction. |
| **mbarrier wait (K/V ready)** | 4 | `SYNCS.PHASECHK.TRANS64.TRYWAIT P0,[base+0x28830]` (K) and `[+0x28850]` (V), each = 1 try + 1 retry; on fail `@!P0 BRA` to a NANOSLEEP spin trampoline. |
| **mbarrier arrive (buffer free)** | 2 | `SYNCS.ARRIVE.TRANS64.RED.A1T0 [.+0x28840/0x28860]` → releases K/V smem back to producer. |
| **wgmma fence** | 2 | `WARPGROUP.ARRIVE` (= wgmma.fence.sync) before the QK burst and before the PV burst. |
| **wgmma wait** | 2 | `WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1` (= wgmma.wait_group<1>, keeps 1 group in flight for overlap). |
| **named-barrier (ping-pong)** | 2 | `BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING R18,0x100` + `BAR.ARV R21,0x100` — 0x100=256 threads = the two consumer warpgroups alternating softmax↔GEMM. |
| int/uniform addr math + BRA | ~180 | UIADD3/UMOV/ULEA computing smem matrix-descriptor offsets, 6 BRA (incl. the latch). |

### Issue order (one steady-state iteration)
```
SYNCS.PHASECHK…TRYWAIT [K@0x28830]      ; wait K tile (spin+NANOSLEEP on miss)
BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING R18, 0x100      ; ping-pong barrier
WARPGROUP.ARRIVE                        ; wgmma fence
8× HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24,gdesc…  ; QK^T burst (interleaved only with UIADD3 desc math)
SYNCS.PHASECHK…TRYWAIT [V@0x28850]      ; wait V tile
WARPGROUP.ARRIVE
8× HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R88,R1xx,gdesc[..].tnspB  ; P·V burst (P in regs)
BAR.ARV R21, 0x100                      ; release sibling warpgroup
WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE gsb0, 0x1           ; wgmma.wait_group<1>
SYNCS.ARRIVE…RED  [K/V empty]           ; free smem → producer
── softmax block ──  FMNMX×68 → MUFU.EX2×66 → FADD×64 → FMUL/FFMA → F2FP×32 → SHFL.BFLY×4
BRA 0x6980/0xb8d0                       ; latch
```
**exp2 does not interleave between individual HGMMA.** The 16 wgmma are issued as two back-to-back async bursts; the entire 66-EX2 / 266-FP32 softmax then runs *in the shadow* of the async tensor pipe. `wgmma.wait_group<1>` leaves one group in flight so iter *i+1*'s QK overlaps iter *i*'s softmax (IntraWGOverlap). Representative QK burst (note pure UIADD3 filler, no math between mmas):
```
/*bab0*/ WARPGROUP.ARRIVE ;
/*bae0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, gdesc[UR16], RZ, !UPT ;
/*baf0*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, gdesc[UR20], R24 ;
/*bb40*/ HGMMA.64x128x16.F32.BF16 R24, gdesc[UR20], R24 ;   … ×8
```

### Producer loop D — how paged cp.async is issued (page_size=1 ⇒ non-TMA)
LDGSTS come in **128-bit pairs**, all `LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.LTC128B.128` (16-byte, generic/`.E`, **L1-bypass straight to smem**, L2 128-byte-sector hint), **gather-addressed** — each token's address is built per-row (`SHFL.IDX` broadcasts the per-token page pointer, then `LEA/IMAD.X` forms the 64-bit global address), which is exactly why TMA can't be used at page_size=1:
```
/*122a0*/ @P0 LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.LTC128B.128 [R25+0x1ac00], desc[UR28][R2.64],      !P2 ;
/*122b0*/ @P0 LDGSTS.E.BYPASS.LTC128B.128 [R25+0x1ec00], desc[UR28][R2.64+0x80], !P1 ;
/*122d0*/ SHFL.IDX PT, R2, R14, 0x6, 0x181f ;      ; gather next page ptr
…
/*124b0*/ @!P6 ARRIVES.LDGSTSBAR.64.TRANSCNT [UR4+0x28830] ;  ; commit cp.async bytes → K mbarrier
/*124c0*/ @P0  BRA.U.ANY 0x12470 ;
```
80 static LDGSTS in the producer body (K into smem `…+0x1ac00/b400/bc00`, V into `…+0x1ec00/f400/fc00`), `@P0`-predicated for varlen/seqlen tails. Completion is published to the **same mbarrier the consumer polls** (base `+0x28830` for K, `+0x28850` for V) via `ARRIVES.LDGSTSBAR.64.TRANSCNT` (cp.async-group→mbarrier transaction count, 5 of them). Producer↔consumer handshake uses `TRANS64` mbarriers: producer `ARRIVES.LDGSTSBAR`(full) / consumer `SYNCS.PHASECHK…TRYWAIT`(wait) → consumer `SYNCS.ARRIVE…RED`(empty) / producer waits to refill.

### Why the tensor pipe sits at ~75%
Per interior iteration the tensor cores execute **16 HGMMA** while the CUDA/MUFU pipes must retire **66 EX2 + 266 FP32 ALU + 32 F2FP + 4 SHFL** (~370 math ops) plus ~180 address/control ops — only ~3% of issued instructions are HGMMA. The softmax is largely hidden by wgmma-async + the WG0/WG1 ping-pong (`BAR` on 256 threads) + `wgmma.wait_group<1>` double-buffering, but its serial dependency chain (row-max → subtract → `MUFU.EX2` → row-sum → rescale, gated by `WARPGROUP.DEPBAR.LE` before the correction) plus the per-tile `SYNCS.PHASECHK` KV waits leave a ~25% bubble in the HGMMA stream. On causal-diagonal blocks the masked loop (A) adds 132 FSEL + 128 ISETP.GT + 64 LDC.64 (col-index/`-INF` masking), inflating the body to 1266 instrs for the same 16 HGMMA — but those run for only the ~1–2 diagonal blocks per query tile, so loop B dominates steady-state utilization.
